title: Valid Parentheses
statement:
Check whether the brackets in each line of code are valid. A line is valid when every opening bracket `(`, `[`, or `{` is closed by a bracket of the same kind, and the pairs close in the right order: `f(a[i])` is valid, but `f(a[i)]` and `f(a[i]` are not. The other characters (letters, digits, spaces, and operators) don't matter, so a line with no brackets at all is valid.

The first line is the count `n`. Each of the next `n` lines is one line of code, which may contain spaces. For each one, print `true` when its brackets are valid and `false` otherwise, one answer per line.

Input:

```text
5
print(nums[0])
if (x > 0) { y = [1, 2] }
f(a[i)]
total = (a + b
x = y)
```

Expected output:

```text
true
true
false
false
false
```

hints: Keep the opening brackets you haven't closed yet on a stack. The one on top is the one that has to close next.
At a closing bracket, peek at the top of the stack. The line fails when the stack is empty or the top is a different kind. Otherwise pop it.
At the end of the line, every bracket was closed only if the stack is empty again.
